newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LAWYER FOR MARADONA'S MANAGER SLAMS SECRET WITNESS.
newsitem.headline: LAWYER FOR MARADONA'S MANAGER SLAMS SECRET WITNESS.

text.p: The lawyer for Argentine soccer star Diego Maradona's manager Guillermo Coppola on Thursday dismissed testimony by a secret witness that his client paid young women to smuggle cocaine into Europe.
Lawyer Mariano Cuneo Liberona repeated Coppola's claim he was framed in a drug bust last week and said testimonies do not carry the same weight when a witness' identity is secret.

"They don't have the same impact. The person can't be charged with false testimony and you can't know if such a witness is a witness I'm suing in another court for lying," Cuneo Liberona told local radio.
The newspaper Daily Clarin on Thursday said that one of Coppola's former girlfriends testified he paid attractive young women $15,000 a time to smuggle cocaine into Europe, usually into Spain.

Quoting court sources, Clarin said the woman told investigators that Coppola kept a pound (500 grams) of drugs for himself out of each shipment he received. The cocaine not smuggled to Europe was distributed in Buenos Aires.
But Cuneo Liberona, who said he did not know who the witness was, brushed aside the declarations, dismissing them as "full of subjectivity."
Saying he could provide evidence that drugs were planted in Coppola's flat, the lawyer added that the amount of cocaine involved did not warrant drug smuggling charges.

"There have been rulings by the federal court that the quantity of half a kilo (one pound) is for personal use," he said, adding that he thought that Coppola would be a free man by now if he had not been a celebrity.

Coppola handed himself into the police after a day on the run last on Wednesday, when investigators found a pound (500 g) of cocaine in a flower vase in a pre-dawn raid at his luxury Buenos Aires apartment. He faces between four and 15 years in prison if found guilty of drug-smuggling charges.

Coppola's permanent tan and white hair have appeared regularly in Argentine glossy magazines and social pages for years, as a leading member of an Argentine jet-set of sports stars, models, actors and politicians.

But one of Coppola's glamorous friendships, with former Argentine national soccer team player Alberto Tarantini, may be in danger. Tarantini, also being held on drug-smuggling charges, was accused on Tuesday of informing on Coppola by the wife of another man caught in last week's drug swoop.

Some Maradona fans blame Coppola for their idol's drug habit, which earned him a 15-month suspension after a dope test in the U.S. World Cup. Maradona has admitted his drug problem and went to a Swiss clinic last month, but a few days later he smashed up a Spanish hotel and was then accused of switching urine tests after a random post-match drug test.
